title: Google's Open-Source Bug Bounty Program Has A Big AI Problem
key_facts: BGR says many bug bounty programmes have been overwhelmed by low-quality, LLM-generated reports that often describe fictitious or hallucinated vulnerabilities.
Google suspended its paid Open Source Software Vulnerability Reporting Program (OSS VRP), which previously paid up to $31,337 for the most serious flaws.
BGR says Curl, Intel and HackerOne have also suspended paid programmes (BGR's claim; Intel's top reward was up to $150,000).
Google says the vast majority of automated submissions are not valid and has committed to reformatting the programme and giving an update in the first quarter of 2027.
Google's other vulnerability reward programme and Patch Rewards programme remain active.
BGR adds opinion about AI-generated content and says AI recently identified over 1,000 vulnerabilities in Linux (unattributed).
quote_evidence: Google says that while the vast majority of automated submissions aren't valid, it has committed to reformatting the program and providing an update in the first quarter of 2027.
In the meantime, bounty hunters are encouraged to continue submitting reports to Google's other VRP or Patch Rewards programs, which remain active.
why_it_matters_hint: Google's pause on paid open-source bug reports shows AI-generated spam straining security reporting; it is a commentary repeat of a story we carried on 5 Oct 2026.
notes: BGR is a commentary piece repeating the pause we carried on 5 Oct 2026 (C12-04 of that day, from TechCrunch, which quotes Google); no new fact. BGR names the programme 'Open Source Software Vulnerability Reporting Program'; TechCrunch's name was 'Rewards Program'.
